<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   - This is primarily a front-end JavaScript library and demo application (“TalkingHead”) for real-time 3D avatars that speak and lip-sync in the browser.  
   - It provides a core ES-module (`modules/talkinghead.mjs`) plus auxiliary modules for lip-sync, dynamic bones, and audio playback. It loads 3D models (GLB), animations (FBX), audio assets and integrates with external TTS/AI services via HTTP/WebSocket proxies.

2. Analyze the file structure  
   Top-level components:  
   • index.html + siteconfig.js – the test/demo web app UI and configuration  
   • modules/ – ES modules: core TalkingHead class, lipsync-xx, dynamicbones, playback worklet  
   • examples/ – standalone HTML demos showing different integrations (Azure, MP3, minimal)  
   • avatars/, animations/, poses/, audio/, images/, fonts/ – static assets (models, FBX, audio, textures, fonts)  
   • blender/ – Python scripts for offline asset preparation (bone/shape-key renaming, viseme generation)  
   • README.md – detailed project overview, API reference, usage patterns  
   • siteconfig.js – demo app resource URLs, API proxy endpoints  

3. Insights from README  
   - Core features: real-time TTS + word-level timestamps for lip-sync in multiple languages, dynamic bones physics, external TTS/A.I. service integrations  
   - Architecture: module-based, dynamic imports via importmap, uses ThreeJS/WebGL for rendering, Web Audio API + AudioWorklet for low-latency audio  
   - Extensibility: pluggable lipsync modules, dynamic bones config, custom poses/gestures, streaming interface  

4. How to draw the system design diagram  
   a. Main components to represent  
      1. Client-side (Browser)  
         • UI Layer (index.html + controls)  
         • Importmap/ES Module Loader  
         • TalkingHead Core Module (talkinghead.mjs)  
         • Lip-sync Modules (lipsync-en.mjs, fi, lt)  
         • Dynamic Bones Module  
         • Playback Worklet (playback-worklet.js)  
         • ThreeJS Renderer & Scene Graph  
         • Asset Loader (GLTFLoader, FBXLoader)  
         • Web Audio API + GainNodes + AudioWorklet  
         • Configuration (siteconfig.js)  
         • Static Assets (avatars/, animations/, poses/, audio/, images/, fonts/)  
      2. Offline Asset Pipeline  
         • Blender Scripts (blender/*.py)  
         • Asset preparation & export (GLB, FBX, viseme blendshapes)  
      3. Proxy Layer (hosted by the integrator; not in repo)  
         • HTTP(S)/WebSocket proxy endpoints (e.g., /gtts/, /openai/v1/, /elevenlabs/)  
      4. External Services  
         • Google Cloud TTS  
         • Microsoft Azure Speech SDK (WebSocket)  
         • ElevenLabs TTS (WebSocket)  
         • OpenAI / Vertex AI / Grok / local llama.cpp / whisper-web  

   b. Relationships & data flows  
      - Browser UI → module loader → TalkingHead core  
      - TalkingHead invokes Asset Loader → pulls GLB/FBX → populates ThreeJS scene  
      - User triggers speakText() or streamStart() → TalkingHead sends HTTP/WebSocket requests to proxy endpoints  
      - Proxy forwards to external TTS/AI service → returns audio + timestamps/visemes/blendshapes → TalkingHead receives via Fetch or WebSocket  
      - TalkingHead audio buffer → Web Audio API / AudioWorklet for playback  
      - Word/viseme timing → drive morph targets / dynamic bones physics → ThreeJS render loop  
      - Offline: Blender scripts process custom models → export into avatars/ and animations/  

   c. Architectural patterns & design principles  
      - Module-based ES6 design (clear separation of core, lip-sync, physics, playback)  
      - Event-driven streaming pipeline (speakText queue, streamAudio chunks, callbacks for onSubtitles/onAudioStart)  
      - Separation of concerns: rendering (ThreeJS), audio (Web Audio API), business logic (TalkingHead class), asset preparation (Blender scripts)  
      - Pluggable back-ends: any TTS service providing word-level timestamps or viseme IDs through a proxy layer  
      - Extensibility via data-driven configuration (siteconfig.js, appendices A–G)  

   d. Key technologies & frameworks  
      - JavaScript ES6 Modules + importmap  
      - ThreeJS / WebGL for 3D rendering  
      - GLTFLoader / FBXLoader (+ optional Draco compression)  
      - Web Audio API + GainNode + AudioWorklet  
      - Fetch API and WebSocket API for service calls  
      - Blender Python scripting for offline asset conversion  
      - External services: Google TTS, Azure Speech SDK, ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Vertex AI, Grok, whisper-web  

5. Guidelines for tailoring the diagram to this project  
   - Emphasize the pure front-end nature: all core logic runs in the browser.  
   - Show the demarcation between core library modules and the test/demo app (index.html + siteconfig.js).  
   - Illustrate the role of the proxy layer as a thin pass‐through to external services (not part of the repo, but essential).  
   - Separate runtime components (renderer, audio engine, lip-sync engine, dynamic bones) from offline asset pipeline (Blender scripts).  
   - Highlight pluggable modules—each lipsync language and the dynamic bones engine—as separate boxes feeding into TalkingHead core.  

6. Diagram best practices  
   - Use clear, consistent labels for each component (e.g., “TalkingHead Core”, “ThreeJS Renderer”, “Web Audio Worklet”, “TTS Proxy”).  
   - Draw directional arrows to show:  
     • Module loading & control flow (index.html → TalkingHead)  
     • Asset loading (TalkingHead → avatars/, animations/)  
     • Service calls (TalkingHead → Proxy → External Service → TalkingHead)  
     • Audio & lip-sync flow (AudioWorklet → Web Audio API → render & morph targets)  
   - Apply color coding or distinct shapes:  
     • Blue rectangles for front-end modules  
     • Green cylinders for static assets  
     • Orange parallelograms for proxy endpoints  
     • Gray clouds for external services  
   - Annotate pipelines:  
     • “Fetch/WS → Audio + Timestamps” on service arrows  
     • “Morph Target Update” on animation arrows  
     • “Render Loop @ 30fps” on the ThreeJS rendering arrow  
   - Optionally include a legend for shapes/colors.

By laying out these elements and flows, the diagram will provide a clear, accurate, and detailed architectural overview of the TalkingHead (3D) project—capturing both the in-browser runtime and the offline asset pipeline, as well as integrations with external AI/TTS services.
